results.question: What are the prerequisites for Deep Learning (TDIS22)?
results.expected_answer: 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Computer Science/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering, plus completed Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics for Intelligent Systems and Machine Learning (7.5 credits each) or equivalent; English proficiency.
results.answer: Deep Learning (TDIS22) requires passed courses of at least 90 credits within the major subject Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from the programme Computer Science and Engineering. It also requires completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits), Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), and Machine Learning (7.5 credits), or equivalent, plus proof of English proficiency.

results.question: How is TARI29 graded?
results.expected_answer: 5, 4, 3 or U; final grade only after all assessments are completed.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, valid from 2025-09-01) is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. The final grade is based on a balanced set of assessments and is only issued after satisfactory completion of all assessments, which include an Examination (5 credits) and an Assignment (2.5 credits) [1].

results.question: What grading scale does the Communication and Artificial Intelligence course use?
results.expected_answer: A, B, C, D, E, FX or F; A to E are passing grades.
results.answer: The Communication and Artificial Intelligence course (LAIK15) is graded A, B, C, D, E, FX or F, and grades A to E are passing grades [1]. Its group presentation is graded U/G rather than on this scale [5]. The similarly named Communication and AI course (L1CAAM) uses the same grading scale [4].

results.question: What do I need before taking Mathematical Statistics?
results.expected_answer: General entry requirements and completed Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits, or equivalent.
results.answer: To take Mathematical Statistics (TMSK17), you need the general entry requirements and a completed Single Variable Calculus course worth 7.5 credits, or an equivalent [2]. This applies to TMSK17 specifically; other courses may have different prerequisites.

results.question: How is the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence course examined?
results.expected_answer: Active participation in seminars and group discussions, and three assignments; graded 5, 4, 3 or U.
results.answer: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (TAIR22) course is graded 5, 4, 3 or U [3]. Examination consists of active participation in seminars and group discussions plus three assignments: an investigation of a fairness-related ethical challenge in a practical case, and a group presentation and a written assignment debating an ethical topic [3]. The final grade requires satisfactory completion of all assessments [3].

results.question: How is the final project in computer science examined?
results.expected_answer: Written report, oral presentation, opposition on another group's work, and mandatory elements; graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail.
results.answer: The question does not name a course, so this covers two current versions. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25, 2025), the course is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, and opposition to another group's report, and a grade is given only after passing all parts [1]. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXV23, 2024), it is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, a review and discussion of another group's work, and fulfilment of mandatory elements, graded 5/4/3/U [3]. Other courses may differ.

results.question: Does the Deep Learning course include a project?
results.expected_answer: Yes: one project with tutoring and two project seminars (design and final presentation).
results.answer: Yes. The Deep Learning (TDIS22) course includes a project worth 5.5 credits, graded on the project report and presentations [5][1]. The Deep Learning for PhD Students (FT3DLFP) course also includes one project [2]. Other courses may differ.

results.question: Which language is the Artificial Intelligence course TARI29 taught in?
results.expected_answer: English.
results.answer: The Artificial Intelligence course (TARI29) is taught in English [1].

results.question: What topics does TARI29 cover?
results.expected_answer: Traditional AI and search, reasoning under uncertainty, evolutionary optimization, intelligent agents, game theory and minimax, Markov decision processes.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits) covers traditional AI (GOFAI) topics such as production systems, search, planning, expert systems, propositional and predicate logic, and resolution. It also covers reasoning under uncertainty (Bayesian inferencing), evolutionary optimization programming, intelligent agents, basic game theory with minimax, and agents for Markov decision processes [1][2].

results.question: What are the entry requirements for Mathematics for Intelligent Systems?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, IT or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, including at least 15 credits of mathematics.
results.answer: Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (TMAR21) requires a minimum bachelor's degree (180 ECTS credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, Information Technology or Electrical Engineering (with relevant computer engineering courses), or equivalent. The bachelor's degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required.

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work in Computer Science (TEXV23) be waived?
results.expected_answer: The programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements, but not from the required Bachelor degree.
results.answer: Yes, the programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements under Prerequisites for TEXV23. No exemption is made for the required Bachelor degree.

results.question: When can I start my final project work?
results.expected_answer: After the examiner's approval.
results.answer: You may start your final project work once the examiner approves it, according to the syllabi for TEXT25 [1], TEPV25 [2] and TETT23 [4]. Generally, you must meet the course prerequisites and submit the registration form to the course coordinator for examiner approval [3][5]. If you do not receive registration approval within the time set in the study guide, you are referred to the start of the next course [5]. These syllabus rules apply only to the named courses, and other courses may differ.

results.question: Which courses must I have taken before Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving?
results.expected_answer: Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, among the listed courses, plus 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: To take Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving (TIOS26), you need either at least 90 credits passed in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or at least 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering. You also need Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Knowledge Representation and the Semantic Web (7.5 credits), or equivalent courses, plus proof of English proficiency.

results.question: How is the final grade decided in Deep Learning?
results.expected_answer: Graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail; project credits come from the report, two presentations and active participation in two seminars.
results.answer: In Deep Learning (TDIS22), the final grade is determined by the two presentations and the project report, and the grade is 5, 4, 3 or Fail [1]. The project report grade reflects both the collaborative and individual parts [1]. The course grade is issued only when all course units have been passed [2].

results.question: What kind of teaching does Data Science Programming have?
results.expected_answer: Lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, in English.
results.answer: Data Science Programming (TDPS22) teaching consists of lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, and is conducted in English [1].

results.question: What happens if I am late to my exam?
results.expected_answer: Doors are closed and locked 10 minutes before the exam starts; be on site no later than 10 minutes before.
results.answer: If you arrive late, the doors are locked 10 minutes before the exam, so you will not be admitted and must wait for the second admission at 9:30 AM or 2:30 PM [2]. Once 30 minutes of the exam have passed, an invigilator will check your ID, give brief instructions, and assign your seat [1]. If you arrive more than 30 minutes late, you will not be allowed to take the exam, and no excuses are accepted [1].

results.question: How many days before an exam must I register?
results.expected_answer: No later than 10 days before; unregistered students cannot take the exam.
results.answer: You must register no later than 10 days before the examination date. Registration can be done via StudentLadok or the JU Mobile app. [1]

results.question: Which IDs are accepted at exams?
results.expected_answer: Valid Swedish driver's license, Swedish passport, Swedish national ID card, or JU card marked Identity Card; valid foreign passports under conditions.
results.answer: Accepted IDs are a valid Swedish driver's license, a valid Swedish passport, a valid Swedish national ID card, and a valid JU card marked "Identity Card" [1]. Foreign passports must be valid, plastic wrapped, and in English, French, or Spanish [1]. BankID and Freja eID+ are not accepted because they are not physical identification [1].

results.question: Can I identify myself with BankID at an exam?
results.expected_answer: No. BankID and Freja eID+ are not physical identification.
results.answer: No. Identification with BankID or Freja eID+ does not count as physical identification and is not accepted as valid ID during exams. You must show an accepted physical ID, such as a valid Swedish driver's license, passport, national ID card, or a JU card marked "Identity Card".

results.question: Can I bring snacks into the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Food and drinks are allowed, but no nuts, smelly or smudging food, and no fragrances.
results.answer: Yes, you can bring food and drinks into the examination halls, but nuts or any food containing nuts, and food that smells or smudges, are not allowed. [1]

results.question: When am I allowed to leave the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Not during the first 30 minutes.
results.answer: You may not leave the exam hall during the first 30 minutes [1]. After that, you may leave only for restroom visits, and only with an invigilator's permission and by recording your anonymous code and time on the restroom list, or you will be considered to have cancelled your exam [1][2]. When the invigilators announce that time is up, you must stop writing immediately and hand in your work [4].

results.question: How long does it take to get my exam results?
results.expected_answer: Results are reported via Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam, except for special reasons.
results.answer: Exam results are normally notified to students through Ladok no later than 20 working days after the examination occasion. If special reasons exist, results may be given later, but no later than 14 days before the next examination occasion for the course, and students must be notified in writing of the delay.

results.question: Can I keep my student accommodation during a study break?
results.expected_answer: No.
results.answer: No. Students on a study break are not allowed to keep their student accommodation [1].

results.question: What does a study break mean for my residence permit?
results.expected_answer: JU informs the Migration Agency, which revokes the residence permit, so the student must leave Sweden.
results.answer: Jönköping University informs the Swedish Migration Agency that the student has been granted a study break, and the Swedish Migration Agency will revoke the student's residence permit, so the student must leave Sweden. [1]

results.question: What disciplinary measures can be taken against a student?
results.expected_answer: Warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension; expulsion is also possible.
results.answer: The Disciplinary Committee can issue a warning, exclusion from examinations, or suspension [2]. Exclusion from examinations may not exceed six months in a continuous period, and suspension may not exceed six months in total [2]. The Committee can also expel a student from education at the University, which means they cannot continue their education until further notice [1][2].

results.question: Which decisions can I appeal to the Board of Appeals?
results.expected_answer: Disciplinary Committee decisions (warning, suspension, expulsion) and listed faculty/school decisions.
results.answer: You can appeal Disciplinary Committee warnings or suspensions, and faculty decisions to reject an applicant for not meeting entry requirements, to not waive entry requirements, to refuse deferred enrolment, on transferring credits, to refuse a degree or course certificate, or to withdraw admission due to incorrect information from the applicant [1]. You can also appeal faculty refusals of exemption from a compulsory element, leave from studies, or withdrawal of doctoral supervision [1], and refusals of tuition fee refunds based on special circumstances [2]. Disciplinary appeals must be submitted in writing to the Committee within three weeks, and the 2018 instructions say Committee expulsion decisions may not be appealed, which conflicts with the 2023 list that includes them [4].

results.question: How do I pay the application fee for a local admission?
results.expected_answer: To JU, by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) via the web payment system.
results.answer: For local admissions, the application fee is paid to JU, either by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) through the web-based payment solution in the web application form, or in another manner agreed with JU. It must be paid no later than the deadline for supplementary information. [1]

results.question: What does § 5 of the disciplinary committee instructions say?
results.expected_answer: The disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension.
results.answer: Section 5 lists three disciplinary measures: warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension [1]. A warning is a written notice of the Committee's decision [1]. Exclusion from examinations bars participation in University examinations for a continuous period of up to six months, while suspension bars attending classes, examinations or other education activities for one or more periods totalling up to six months [1]. Any decision on these measures must include the grounds for the decision [1].

results.question: What does section 2.15 of the education regulations say about grades?
results.expected_answer: Results are notified via Ladok within 20 working days of the examination.
results.answer: Section 2.15 says exam results must be notified to students through Ladok within 20 working days of the exam. If special reasons apply, the deadline can be later, but no later than 14 days before the next exam occasion, and students must be told in writing. Feedback must be offered no later than 14 days before the next ordinary exam occasion. Grade notifications must protect students' legal rights and integrity and reach the correct student.

results.question: What are the TARI29 entry requirements?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering, or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: For Artificial Intelligence (TARI29), applicants need a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering (with relevant computer engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering. The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics. Proof of English proficiency is also required.

results.question: What is LAIK15 about?
results.expected_answer: Media and communication and artificial intelligence, including representations of AI and generative AI in media.
results.answer: Communication and Artificial Intelligence (LAIK15) is a 7.5-credit first-cycle course in Media and Communication Science, valid from Spring 2025. It covers research perspectives on artificial intelligence, media and cultural industries, generative AI as a tool for producing texts, representations of AI, and its impact in different contexts [3][4]. Students learn to describe and identify AI representations, explain how generative AI is used, and critically reflect on its opportunities and limitations [5][1].

results.question: Is TDPS22 taught in English?
results.expected_answer: Yes.
results.answer: Yes, Data Science Programming (TDPS22) is taught in English.

results.question: What does § 28 of the disciplinary committee instructions allow?
results.expected_answer: A decision may always be appealed to the Board of Appeals if it contravenes the Discrimination Act.
results.answer: Section 28 allows a decision to be appealed to the Board of Appeals at any time, on the ground that the decision contravenes specified provisions of the Discrimination Act (2008:567): Chapter 2 § 5, with reference to Chapter 1 §§ 4 and 5, and Chapter 3 § 15.

results.question: Can I take Machine Learning (TMLS22) if my major is Computer Science?

results.answer: Possibly. You need at least 90 credits passed within the major subject Computer Science (or another listed major), plus completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), or equivalent courses [2]. You also need proof of English proficiency [2]. If you meet these conditions, you can apply for TMLS22 [2].

The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics. Proof of English proficiency is also required.

results.question: What are the current prerequisites for Deep Learning?
results.expected_answer: As in the 2025 syllabus (valid from 2025-01-01).
results.answer: For Deep Learning (TDIS22), the current version (valid from 2025-01-01) requires passed courses of at least 90 credits within the major subject Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from the Computer Science and Engineering programme.
